newsitem.title: USA: Investigators concerned over Feb. 5 air incident.
newsitem.headline: Investigators concerned over Feb. 5 air incident.

text.p: Investigators said on Tuesday that a Feb. 5 incident in which an airliner made an evasive dive to avoid nearby Air Force planes clearly raised potential safety concerns and needs further investigation.

"The potential for very unfortunate results was clearly there ... There clearly was miscommunicaton or a lack of communication between military air controllers and the flight of F16s," Jim Hall, chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board, said at a news conference on the mid-air episode involving a Nations Air Boeing 727 charter jet and Air National guard planes off the coast of New Jersey on Feb. 5

"Our investigation continues. The military has implemented procedural changes," Hall said. He added that the safety board expected its own investigators to provide it with further safety recommendations within the next 10 days.

Hall noted that three other reported mid-air brushes between military jets and civilian planes had occurred on Feb. 7 over Delaware, Texas and New Mexico. But he said investigation showed no one was endangered in those episodes and they were "not in the same category as the incident involving the Nations Air aircraft."

"It seemed that we were experiencing an epidemic of incidents that seemed to raise concerns," he said, adding that that had not proven to be the case. He also said checks indicated there had been "relatively few instances of dangerous encounters between military and civilian aircraft."

In the Feb. 5 New Jersey incident, the Nations Air pilot manoeuvred violently to evade two Air National Guard F16s in response to electronic cockpit instrument warnings indicating the planes were too close. The Air National Guard commander, Maj. Gen. Donald Shepperd, said at the time that "there was no imminent collision."
